result = Broker.CALCULATE(
    num_customers=COUNT(
        Customers.WHERE(
            ENDSWITH(email, '.com') & 
            HAS(
                transactions_made.WHERE(
                    CONTAINS(ticker.symbol, 'AMZN') |
                    CONTAINS(ticker.symbol, 'AAPL') |
                    CONTAINS(ticker.symbol, 'GOOGL') |
                    CONTAINS(ticker.symbol, 'META') |
                    CONTAINS(ticker.symbol, 'NFLX')
                )
            ) == 1
        )
    )
)

# Get transactions from the last 8 weeks excluding current week
# First, calculate the start of the current week (Monday)
current_week_start = DATETIME('now', 'start of week')

# Calculate 8 weeks ago from the start of current week
eight_weeks_ago = DATETIME(current_week_start, '-56 days')

# Filter transactions for the last 8 weeks excluding current week
recent_transactions = Transactions.WHERE(
    (date_time >= eight_weeks_ago) & 
    (date_time < current_week_start)
).CALCULATE(
    # Calculate week start (Monday) for each transaction
    week_start = DATETIME(date_time, 'start of week'),
    # Check if transaction occurred on weekend (Saturday=7, Sunday=1 in DAYOFWEEK)
    is_weekend = ISIN(DAYOFWEEK(date_time), (1, 7))
)

# Group by week and calculate counts
result = recent_transactions.PARTITION(
    name="weeks", 
    by=week_start
).CALCULATE(
    week_start = week_start,
    total_transactions = COUNT(Transactions),
    weekend_transactions = SUM(Transactions.CALCULATE(is_weekend_int = IFF(is_weekend, 1, 0)).is_weekend_int)
).ORDER_BY(week_start.ASC())

# Define the time boundaries for the analysis.
# The period covers the 8 weeks leading up to the current week.
# 'start of week' defaults to Monday, matching the requirement.
time_boundaries = Broker.CALCULATE(
    start_of_current_week=DATETIME('now', 'start of week'),
    start_of_period=DATETIME('now', 'start of week', '-8 weeks')
)

# Filter transactions to include only stocks within the specified 8-week period.
# Pre-calculate the start date of the week for each transaction and a flag to identify weekend transactions.
stock_transactions_in_period = time_boundaries.Transactions.WHERE(
    (LOWER(ticker.ticker_type) == 'stock') &
    (date_time >= start_of_period) &
    (date_time < start_of_current_week)
).CALCULATE(
    week_start_date=DATETIME(date_time, 'start of week'),
    is_weekend=ISIN(DAYNAME(date_time), ('Saturday', 'Sunday'))
)

# Partition the filtered transactions by the week's start date to group them.
# For each week, calculate the total number of transactions and the count of weekend transactions.
weekly_stock_summary = stock_transactions_in_period.PARTITION(
    name='weekly_groups',
    by=(week_start_date,)
).CALCULATE(
    week_start=week_start_date,
    total_transactions=COUNT(Transactions),
    weekend_transactions=SUM(Transactions.is_weekend)
).ORDER_BY(week_start.ASC())

result = weekly_stock_summary

# First, filter the transactions to include only stocks that occurred in the last 8 weeks, excluding the current week.
# For each of these transactions, we calculate the start date of its week and determine if it occurred on a weekend.
transaction_info = Transactions.WHERE(
    (LOWER(ticker.ticker_type) == 'stock') &
    (date_time >= DATETIME(DATETIME('now', 'start of week'), '-8 weeks')) &
    (date_time < DATETIME('now', 'start of week'))
).CALCULATE(
    week_start_date=DATETIME(date_time, 'start of week'),
    is_weekend=ISIN(DAYNAME(date_time), ("Saturday", "Sunday"))
)

# For each weekly group, we count the total number of transactions and sum the 'is_weekend' flags to get the weekend transaction count.
# The final result is ordered by the week's start date.
weekly_transaction_counts = transaction_info.PARTITION(name="weeks", by=(week_start_date)).CALCULATE(
    week_start_date=week_start_date,
    total_transactions=COUNT(Transactions),
    weekend_transactions=SUM(Transactions.is_weekend)
).ORDER_BY(week_start_date.ASC())

    (date_time >= eight_weeks_ago) & 
    (date_time < current_week_start)
).CALCULATE(
    # Calculate week start (Monday) for each transaction
    week_start = DATETIME(date_time, 'start of week'),
    # Check if transaction occurred on weekend (Saturday=7, Sunday=1 in DAYOFWEEK)
    is_weekend = ISIN(DAYOFWEEK(date_time), (1, 7))
)

# Group by week and calculate counts
result = recent_transactions.PARTITION(
    name="weeks", 
    by=week_start
).CALCULATE(
    week_start = week_start,
    total_transactions = COUNT(Transactions),
    weekend_transactions = SUM(Transactions.CALCULATE(is_weekend_int = IFF(is_weekend, 1, 0)).is_weekend_int)
).ORDER_BY(week_start.ASC())

# Get customers who signed up in the last 6 months excluding current month
# First, let's calculate the date range
recent_customers = Customers.WHERE(
    (join_date >= DATETIME('now', 'start of month', '-6 months')) &
    (join_date < DATETIME('now', 'start of month'))
).CALCULATE(
    signup_month = JOIN_STRINGS('-', YEAR(join_date), LPAD(MONTH(join_date), 2, '0'))
)

# Partition by signup month to calculate PMCS and PMAT
result = recent_customers.PARTITION(name='months', by=signup_month).CALCULATE(
    month = signup_month,
    PMCS = COUNT(Customers),
    PMAT = AVG(Customers.transactions_made.amount)
).ORDER_BY(month.ASC())

    start_of_current_month=DATETIME('now', 'start of month'),
    start_of_period=DATETIME('now', 'start of month', '-6 months')
).Customers.WHERE(

).CALCULATE(

# Get customers who joined in the last 6 months excluding current month
# Calculate the date range: from 6 months ago to the start of current month
recent_customers = Customers.WHERE(
    (join_date >= DATETIME('now', '-6 months', 'start of month')) &
    (join_date < DATETIME('now', 'start of month'))
).CALCULATE(
    join_month = JOIN_STRINGS('-', YEAR(join_date), LPAD(MONTH(join_date), 2, '0'))
)

# Partition by join month to get customer signups per month
monthly_signups = recent_customers.PARTITION(name='months', by=join_month).CALCULATE(
    month = join_month,
    pmcs = COUNT(Customers)
)

# For PMAT, we need to calculate average transaction amount per month
# Get all transactions from these recent customers
customer_transactions = recent_customers.transactions_made.CALCULATE(
    transaction_month = JOIN_STRINGS('-', YEAR(date_time), LPAD(MONTH(date_time), 2, '0')),
    transaction_amount = amount
)

# Partition transactions by month and calculate average
monthly_transactions = customer_transactions.PARTITION(name='tx_months', by=transaction_month).CALCULATE(
    month = transaction_month,
    pmat = AVG(transactions_made.amount)
)

# Combine the results - we need to join PMCS and PMAT by month
# Since we need both metrics for each month, let's use a different approach
# Calculate both metrics in one query by partitioning customers by join month

result = recent_customers.PARTITION(name='signup_months', by=join_month).CALCULATE(
    month = join_month,
    pmcs = COUNT(Customers),
    pmat = AVG(Customers.transactions_made.amount)
).ORDER_BY(month.ASC())

# Step 1: Filter for customers who joined in 2022 and have transactions.
# A new field 'is_active_customer' is created to flag active customers (status is 'active').
customers_info = Customers.WHERE(
    (YEAR(join_date) == 2022) & (HAS(transactions_made) == 1)
).CALCULATE(
    country=country,
    is_active_customer=IFF(LOWER(status) == 'active', 1, 0)
)

# Step 2: Partition the filtered customers by country.
# For each country, calculate the Activity Ratio (AR) using the provided formula.
# The number of active customers is the sum of 'is_active_customer', and the total
# is the count of all customers in that group.
activity_ratio_by_country = customers_info.PARTITION(
    name="country_groups", by=country
).CALCULATE(
    country=country,
    AR=(100.0 * SUM(customers_info.is_active_customer) / COUNT(customers_info))
)

# Filter customers who joined in 2022 and have at least one transaction.
customers_filtered = Customers.WHERE(
    (YEAR(join_date) == 2022) & (HAS(transactions_made) == 1)
)

# Partition the filtered customers by country to calculate metrics for each group.
result = customers_filtered.PARTITION(
    name="country_groups", by=(country)
).CALCULATE(
    # For each country, count the total number of customers and the number of active customers.
    country=country,
    active_customers_count=COUNT(Customers.WHERE(LOWER(status) == 'active')),
    total_customers_count=COUNT(Customers)
).CALCULATE(
    # Calculate the Activity Ratio (AR) and select the final fields.
    # The IFF function prevents division by zero.
    country=country,
    AR=IFF(total_customers_count > 0, (100.0 * active_customers_count) / total_customers_count, 0)
)

# Step 1: Extract month and symbol from daily prices
price_info = DailyPrices.CALCULATE(
    symbol = ticker.symbol,
    month = JOIN_STRINGS("-", YEAR(date), LPAD(MONTH(date), 2, "0")),
    close = close,
    high = high,
    low = low
)

# Step 2: Partition by symbol and month to calculate monthly statistics
monthly_stats = price_info.PARTITION(
    name="symbol_month", 
    by=(symbol, month)
).CALCULATE(
    symbol = symbol,
    month = month,
    avg_close = AVG(DailyPrices.close),
    max_high = MAX(DailyPrices.high),
    min_low = MIN(DailyPrices.low)
)

# Step 3: Calculate MoMC using PREV to get previous month's average
result = monthly_stats.CALCULATE(
    symbol = symbol,
    month = month,
    avg_close = avg_close,
    max_high = max_high,
    min_low = min_low,
    prev_avg_close = PREV(avg_close, by=(symbol.ASC(), month.ASC()), per="Broker", default=0),
    momc = IFF(
        PREV(avg_close, by=(symbol.ASC(), month.ASC()), per="Broker", default=0) == 0,
        0,
        (avg_close - PREV(avg_close, by=(symbol.ASC(), month.ASC()), per="Broker", default=0)) / PREV(avg_close, by=(symbol.ASC(), month.ASC()), per="Broker", default=0)
    )
).CALCULATE(
    symbol,
    month,
    avg_close,
    max_high,
    min_low,
    momc
).ORDER_BY(symbol.ASC(), month.ASC())

    ticker_symbol=ticker_symbol,
    month=month_key,
    avg_close=AVG(DailyPrices.close),
    max_high=MAX(DailyPrices.high),
    min_low=MIN(DailyPrices.low)

    momc=IFF(

)

# Step 3: Calculate MoMC using PREV to get previous month's average
result = monthly_stats.CALCULATE(
    symbol = symbol,
    month = month,
    avg_close = avg_close,
    max_high = max_high,
    min_low = min_low,
    prev_avg_close = PREV(avg_close, by=(symbol.ASC(), month.ASC()), per="symbol", default=0),
    momc = IFF(
        prev_avg_close > 0,
        (avg_close - prev_avg_close) / prev_avg_close,
        0
    )
).WHERE(prev_avg_close > 0)  # Filter out first month for each symbol since it has no previous month

# Step 1: Prepare the daily price data by extracting the symbol and creating a sortable month string (YYYY-MM).
price_info = DailyPrices.CALCULATE(
    symbol=ticker.symbol,
    month_str=JOIN_STRINGS("-", YEAR(date), LPAD(MONTH(date), 2, "0"))
)

# Step 2: Partition by symbol and month to calculate the monthly aggregate statistics.
monthly_stats = price_info.PARTITION(name="ticker_months", by=(symbol, month_str)).CALCULATE(
    symbol=symbol,
    month=month_str,
    avg_close=AVG(DailyPrices.close),
    max_high=MAX(DailyPrices.high),
    min_low=MIN(DailyPrices.low)
)

# Step 3: Partition the monthly statistics by symbol to create groups for the window function.
ticker_groups = monthly_stats.PARTITION(name="tickers", by=symbol)

# Step 4: For each ticker group, calculate the month-over-month change (MoMC) using the PREV window function.
# The PREV function looks at the previous month's average close within the same ticker group.
result = ticker_groups.ticker_months.CALCULATE(
    symbol=symbol,
    month=month,
    average_closing_price=avg_close,
    highest_price=max_high,
    lowest_price=min_low,
    prev_month_avg_close=PREV(avg_close, by=month.ASC(), per="tickers")
).CALCULATE(
    symbol,
    month,
    average_closing_price,
    highest_price,
    lowest_price,
    momc=IFF(
        (prev_month_avg_close != None) & (prev_month_avg_close != 0),
        (average_closing_price - prev_month_avg_close) / prev_month_avg_close,
        None
    )
)

# Step 1: Create a base collection with the necessary calculated fields: ticker symbol and a formatted month string for grouping and sorting.
price_info = DailyPrices.CALCULATE(
    symbol=ticker.symbol,
    month_str=JOIN_STRINGS("-", YEAR(date), LPAD(MONTH(date), 2, "0"))
)

# Step 2: Partition the daily prices by symbol and month to calculate the monthly aggregates.
# This creates a collection where each record contains the stats for a specific ticker in a specific month.
monthly_stats = price_info.PARTITION(name="monthly_groups", by=(symbol, month_str)).CALCULATE(
    symbol=symbol,
    month=month_str,
    avg_close=AVG(DailyPrices.close),
    max_high=MAX(DailyPrices.high),
    min_low=MIN(DailyPrices.low)
)

# Step 3: Partition the monthly stats by symbol. This allows us to use the PREV window function
# to get the previous month's data for each ticker separately.
# The 'per="ticker_groups"' argument in PREV ensures the calculation is contained within each ticker's data.
result = monthly_stats.PARTITION(name="ticker_groups", by=(symbol)).monthly_groups.CALCULATE(
    symbol=symbol,
    month=month,
    average_closing_price=avg_close,
    highest_price=max_high,
    lowest_price=min_low,
    prev_avg_close=PREV(avg_close, by=month.ASC(), per="ticker_groups")
).CALCULATE(
    symbol=symbol,
    month=month,
    average_closing_price=average_closing_price,
    highest_price=highest_price,
    lowest_price=lowest_price,
    # Calculate MoMC, handling cases where the previous month's average is null or zero to avoid errors.
    MoMC=IFF(
        (prev_avg_close == None) | (prev_avg_close == 0),
        None,
        (average_closing_price - prev_avg_close) / prev_avg_close
    )
)

    (date_time >= "2023-01-01") & (date_time <= "2023-03-31")

# Step 1: Filter transactions to the specified date range from Jan 1, 2023, to Mar 31, 2023.
# Using '< "2023-04-01"' is a robust way to include all timestamps on March 31st.
transactions_in_range = Transactions.WHERE(
    (date_time >= "2023-01-01") & (date_time < "2023-04-01")
)

# Step 2: Partition the filtered transactions by their type.
# For each type, calculate the number of distinct customers and the average number of shares.
transaction_type_stats = transactions_in_range.PARTITION(
    name="groups_by_type", by=transaction_type
).CALCULATE(
    transaction_type=transaction_type,
    num_distinct_customers=NDISTINCT(Transactions.customer_id),
    avg_shares=AVG(Transactions.shares)
)

# Step 3: Select the top 3 transaction types based on the number of distinct customers, sorted in descending order.
top_transaction_types = transaction_type_stats.TOP_K(
    3, by=num_distinct_customers.DESC()
)

# First, prepare transaction data with customer state and ticker type
transaction_info = Transactions.CALCULATE(
    customer_state = customer.state,
    ticker_type = ticker.ticker_type
)

# Partition by the combination of customer state and ticker type
state_type_groups = transaction_info.PARTITION(
    name="state_type_combos", 
    by=(customer_state, ticker_type)
).CALCULATE(
    customer_state = customer_state,
    ticker_type = ticker_type,
    num_transactions = COUNT(Transactions)
)

# Get the top 5 combinations
result = state_type_groups.TOP_K(5, by=num_transactions.DESC())

transaction_info = Transactions.CALCULATE(
    customer_state=customer.state,
    ticker_type=ticker.ticker_type
)

# Next, we partition the transaction_info collection by the combination of customer_state and ticker_type.
# For each unique combination, we count the number of transactions.
combinations = transaction_info.PARTITION(
    name="state_ticker_groups",
    by=(customer_state, ticker_type)
).CALCULATE(
    customer_state=customer_state,
    ticker_type=ticker_type,
    num_transactions=COUNT(Transactions)
)

# Finally, we select the top 5 combinations with the highest number of transactions,
# ordering the results in descending order.
result = combinations.TOP_K(5, by=num_transactions.DESC())

# Filter transactions for Q1 2023 and successful status
q1_2023_transactions = Transactions.WHERE(
    (YEAR(date_time) == 2023) & 
    (MONTH(date_time) >= 1) & 
    (MONTH(date_time) <= 3) &
    (LOWER(status) == 'success')
).CALCULATE(
    year = YEAR(date_time),
    month = MONTH(date_time)
)

# Partition by year and month, then calculate average price
result = q1_2023_transactions.PARTITION(
    name="monthly_groups", 
    by=(year, month)
).CALCULATE(
    year = year,
    month = month,
    avg_price = AVG(Transactions.price)
).ORDER_BY(year.ASC(), month.ASC())

successful_q1_transactions = Transactions.WHERE(
    (LOWER(status) == 'success') &
    (YEAR(date_time) == 2023) &
    ISIN(MONTH(date_time), (1, 2, 3))
)

transactions_with_month = successful_q1_transactions.CALCULATE(
    transaction_month=MONTH(date_time)
)

monthly_average_prices = transactions_with_month.PARTITION(
    name="monthly_transactions", by=(transaction_month)
).CALCULATE(
    month=transaction_month,
    average_price=AVG(Transactions.price)
).ORDER_BY(month.ASC())

# Get sales with sale price over $30,000 and their payments
high_value_sales_payments = Sales.WHERE(sale_price > 30000).payment.CALCULATE(
    payment_date=payment_date,
    # Calculate the week start date (Monday) for each payment
    week_start=DATETIME(payment_date, 'start of week'),
    # Determine if payment was on weekend (Saturday=6, Sunday=0 in DAYOFWEEK)
    is_weekend=ISIN(DAYOFWEEK(payment_date), (6, 0))
)

# Filter to only include payments from the last 8 weeks (excluding current week)
# Current week starts at DATETIME('now', 'start of week')
# 8 weeks ago starts at DATETIME('now', 'start of week', '-8 weeks')
filtered_payments = high_value_sales_payments.WHERE(
    (week_start >= DATETIME('now', 'start of week', '-8 weeks')) &
    (week_start < DATETIME('now', 'start of week'))
)

# Group by week and calculate counts
result = filtered_payments.PARTITION(name="weeks", by=week_start).CALCULATE(
    week=week_start,
    total_payments_received=COUNT(payment),
    weekend_payments_received=SUM(is_weekend)
).ORDER_BY(week.ASC())

    # Define the start of the current week, assuming weeks start on Monday.
    start_of_current_week=DATETIME('now', 'start of week'),
    # Define the start of the 8-week period we are interested in.
    start_of_period=DATETIME('now', 'start of week', '-8 weeks')
).Sales.WHERE(

    sale_price > 30000
).payment.WHERE(
    # Filter payments to include only those within the last 8 weeks, excluding the current week.
    (payment_date >= start_of_period) & (payment_date < start_of_current_week)
).CALCULATE(
    # For each payment, determine the start of its week.
    week_start_date=DATETIME(payment_date, 'start of week'),
    # Flag payments that occurred on a weekend (Saturday or Sunday).
    is_weekend=ISIN(DAYNAME(payment_date), ("Saturday", "Sunday"))
).PARTITION(
    # Group the filtered payments by the start date of their week.
    name="weekly_groups", by=(week_start_date)
).CALCULATE(
    # For each weekly group, calculate the required metrics.
    week=week_start_date,
    total_payments_received=COUNT(payment),
    weekend_payments_received=SUM(is_weekend)
).ORDER_BY(
    # Sort the final results by week in ascending order.
    week.ASC()

# Get sales with sale price over $30,000 and their payments
high_value_sales = Sales.WHERE(sale_price > 30000)

# Get all payments for these high-value sales with week information
payments_with_week_info = high_value_sales.payment.CALCULATE(
    payment_date=payment_date,
    # Calculate the start of the week (Monday) for each payment
    week_start=DATETIME(payment_date, 'start of week'),
    # Determine if payment was on weekend (Saturday=6, Sunday=0 in some systems, but let's use DAYNAME)
    is_weekend=IFF(
        (DAYNAME(payment_date) == "Saturday") | (DAYNAME(payment_date) == "Sunday"),
        1,
        0
    )
)

# Filter to only include payments from the last 8 weeks (excluding current week)
# Current week starts at the most recent Monday
current_week_start = DATETIME('now', 'start of week')
eight_weeks_ago = DATETIME(current_week_start, '-56 days')  # 8 weeks * 7 days = 56 days

filtered_payments = payments_with_week_info.WHERE(
    (week_start >= eight_weeks_ago) & (week_start < current_week_start)
)

# Group by week and calculate totals
result = filtered_payments.PARTITION(name="weeks", by=week_start).CALCULATE(
    week=week_start,
    total_payments_received=COUNT(payment),
    weekend_payments_received=SUM(payment.is_weekend)
).ORDER_BY(week.ASC())

# Define the start of the current week and the start of the 8-week analysis period.
start_of_current_week = DATETIME('now', 'start of week')
start_of_period = DATETIME('now', 'start of week', '-8 weeks')

# Filter sales over $30,000, access their payments, and filter for the last 8 weeks.
# Also, calculate the week start date and a weekend flag for each payment.
payments_in_window = Sales.WHERE(sale_price > 30000).payment.WHERE(
    (payment_date >= start_of_period) & (payment_date < start_of_current_week)
).CALCULATE(
    week_start_date=DATETIME(payment_date, 'start of week'),
    is_weekend=IFF(DAYOFWEEK(payment_date) >= 6, 1, 0)
)

# Partition the filtered payments by week and calculate the total and weekend payment counts.
weekly_payment_summary = payments_in_window.PARTITION(
    name="weekly_groups", by=(week_start_date,)
).CALCULATE(
    week=week_start_date,
    total_payments_received=COUNT(PaymentsReceived),
    weekend_payments_received=SUM(PaymentsReceived.is_weekend)
).ORDER_BY(week.ASC())

# Define the start of the current week and the start of the 8-week analysis period.
start_of_current_week = DATETIME('now', 'start of week')
start_of_period = DATETIME('now', 'start of week', '-8 weeks')

# Filter sales over $30,000, access their payments, and filter for the last 8 weeks.
# Also, calculate the week start date and a weekend flag for each payment.
payments_in_window = Sales.WHERE(sale_price > 30000).payment.WHERE(
    (payment_date >= start_of_period) & (payment_date < start_of_current_week)
).CALCULATE(
    week_start_date=DATETIME(payment_date, 'start of week'),
    is_weekend=IFF(DAYOFWEEK(payment_date) >= 6, 1, 0)
)

# Partition the filtered payments by week and calculate the total and weekend payment counts.
weekly_payment_summary = payments_in_window.PARTITION(
    name="weekly_groups", by=(week_start_date,)
).CALCULATE(
    week=week_start_date,
    total_payments_received=COUNT(PaymentsReceived),
    weekend_payments_received=SUM(PaymentsReceived.is_weekend)
).ORDER_BY(week.ASC())

result = weekly_payment_summary

# First, get cars that have been sold and their most recent inventory status
sold_cars_with_status = Cars.WHERE(
    HAS(sale_records) == 1
).CALCULATE(
    car_make = make,
    car_model = model,
    # Get the most recent inventory snapshot for this car
    current_inventory_status = inventory_snapshots.WHERE(
        RANKING(by=snapshot_date.DESC(), per="Cars", allow_ties=False) == 1
    ).SINGULAR().is_in_inventory,
    # Get the maximum sale price for this car
    max_sale_price = MAX(sale_records.sale_price)
)

# Filter for cars that are not in inventory
cars_not_in_inventory = sold_cars_with_status.WHERE(
    current_inventory_status == False
)

# Group by make and model to get the highest sale price for each combination
result = cars_not_in_inventory.PARTITION(
    name="make_model_groups", 
    by=(car_make, car_model)
).CALCULATE(
    make = car_make,
    model = car_model,
    highest_sale_price = MAX(Cars.max_sale_price)
).ORDER_BY(highest_sale_price.DESC())

# Define a contextless expression to get the latest inventory snapshot for each car.
# This uses RANKING to find the snapshot with the most recent date for each car.
latest_inventory_snapshot = Cars.inventory_snapshots.WHERE(
    RANKING(by=snapshot_date.DESC(), per="Cars") == 1
).SINGULAR()

# Filter for cars that have been sold (have sale_records) and are no longer in inventory
# according to their latest snapshot.
sold_and_out_of_stock_cars = Cars.WHERE(
    (HAS(sale_records) == 1) &
    (latest_inventory_snapshot.is_in_inventory == False)
)

# Partition the filtered cars by make and model, then calculate the maximum sale price for each group.
# Finally, order the results by the highest sale price in descending order.
highest_sales_by_make_model = sold_and_out_of_stock_cars.PARTITION(
    name="make_model_groups", by=(make, model)
).CALCULATE(
    make=make,
    model=model,
    highest_sale_price=MAX(Cars.sale_records.sale_price)
).ORDER_BY(highest_sale_price.DESC())

[DEBUG] [Q37] Code generated by gemini:
# Define a contextless expression to efficiently get the latest inventory snapshot for each car.
# This is done by ranking the snapshots by date in descending order for each car and picking the top one.
# SINGULAR() is used to treat the result as a single record, allowing direct field access.
latest_inventory_status = Cars.inventory_snapshots.WHERE(
    RANKING(by=snapshot_date.DESC(), per="Cars") == 1
).SINGULAR()

# Start with the Cars collection and filter for cars that meet two criteria:
# 1. The car has at least one sale record (HAS(sale_records) == 1).
# 2. The car's most recent inventory status is 'not in inventory' (is_in_inventory == False).
sold_and_out_of_stock_cars = Cars.WHERE(
    (HAS(sale_records) == 1) & (latest_inventory_status.is_in_inventory == False)
)

# Partition the filtered cars by make and model to group them.
# For each group, calculate the make, model, and the maximum sale price from all associated sale records.
# Finally, order the results by the highest sale price in descending order.
highest_sales_by_make_model = sold_and_out_of_stock_cars.PARTITION(
    name="car_groups", by=(make, model)
).CALCULATE(
    make=make,
    model=model,
    highest_sale_price=MAX(Cars.sale_records.sale_price)
).ORDER_BY(highest_sale_price.DESC())

# Get the date range for the last 6 months excluding current month
current_month_start = DATETIME('now', 'start of month')
six_months_ago = DATETIME(current_month_start, '-6 months')

# Filter salespersons hired between 2022 and 2023 and get their sales
eligible_sales = Salespersons.WHERE(
    (YEAR(hire_date) >= 2022) & (YEAR(hire_date) <= 2023)
).sales_made.WHERE(
    (sale_date >= six_months_ago) & (sale_date < current_month_start)
).CALCULATE(
    salesperson_id=salesperson.salesperson_id,
    first_name=salesperson.first_name,
    last_name=salesperson.last_name,
    sale_month=DATETIME(sale_date, 'start of month'),
    sale_price=sale_price
)

# Partition by salesperson and month
result = eligible_sales.PARTITION(
    name="monthly_groups",
    by=(salesperson_id, first_name, last_name, sale_month)
).CALCULATE(

    last_name=last_name,
    month=sale_month,

    pmsr=SUM(sales_made.sale_price)  # Per month sales revenue
).ORDER_BY(month.ASC())

# Define the date boundaries for the last 6 months, excluding the current month.
date_boundaries = Dealership.CALCULATE(
    start_date=DATETIME('now', 'start of month', '-6 months'),
    end_date=DATETIME('now', 'start of month')
)

# Filter sales to the specified date range and for salespersons hired in 2022-2023.
# Also, create a 'sale_month' column for grouping.
sales_to_group = date_boundaries.Sales.WHERE(
    (sale_date >= start_date) &
    (sale_date < end_date) &
    (YEAR(salesperson.hire_date) >= 2022) &
    (YEAR(salesperson.hire_date) <= 2023)
).CALCULATE(
    sale_month=DATETIME(sale_date, 'start of month')
)

# Partition the filtered sales by month to calculate the required metrics.
# The result is ordered by month in ascending order.
monthly_summary = sales_to_group.PARTITION(
    name="sales_by_month",
    by=(sale_month)
).CALCULATE(
    month=sale_month,
    PMSPS=COUNT(Sales),
    PMSR=SUM(Sales.sale_price)
).ORDER_BY(month.ASC())

# Define the date range at the top level for access throughout the query.
# This establishes the start (6 months ago) and end (current month) of our window.
date_range_def = Dealership.CALCULATE(
    start_date = DATETIME('now', 'start of month', '-6 months'),
    end_date = DATETIME('now', 'start of month')
)

# Start with all sales and calculate the month of each sale. This creates a "scaffold"
# of all months that have at least one sale, ensuring we can report on months with
# zero sales for our specific salesperson group.
sales_with_month = date_range_def.Sales.CALCULATE(
    sale_month = DATETIME(sale_date, 'start of month')
)

# Partition all sales by the calculated month. This groups all sales into monthly buckets.
monthly_groups = sales_with_month.PARTITION(name="monthly_sales", by=(sale_month))

# For each month group, calculate the required metrics.
# The filtering for salespersons (hired between 2022-2023) is applied *inside*
# the aggregation functions. This is the key to getting 0s for months that have
# sales, but not from the target salesperson group.
monthly_metrics = monthly_groups.CALCULATE(
    month = sale_month,
    # PMSPS: Count sales where the salesperson was hired in the target years.
    PMSPS = COUNT(Sales.WHERE(
        (YEAR(salesperson.hire_date) >= 2022) & (YEAR(salesperson.hire_date) <= 2023)
    )),
    # PMSR: Sum sale_price for the same filtered group. Default to 0.0 if no such sales exist.
    PMSR = DEFAULT_TO(SUM(Sales.WHERE(
        (YEAR(salesperson.hire_date) >= 2022) & (YEAR(salesperson.hire_date) <= 2023)
    ).sale_price), 0.0)
)

# Finally, filter the aggregated monthly results to our desired time window (last 6 months)
# and order them chronologically.
pmsps_and_pmsr_metrics = monthly_metrics.WHERE(
    (month >= start_date) & (month < end_date)
).ORDER_BY(month.ASC())

# Step 1: Create a 'sale_month' column by truncating the 'sale_date' for each sale.
sales_with_month_info = Sales.CALCULATE(
    sale_month=DATETIME(sale_date, 'start of month')
)

# Step 2: Partition all sales by 'sale_month'. This creates a collection where each item represents a month,
# acting as a calendar based on sales data. This assumes at least one sale occurred in each of the last 6 months.
monthly_sales_groups = sales_with_month_info.PARTITION(name="sales_by_month", by=(sale_month))

# Step 3: Filter the monthly groups to the last 6 months (excluding the current month) and calculate metrics.
result = monthly_sales_groups.WHERE(
    (sale_month >= DATETIME('now', 'start of month', '-6 months')) &
    (sale_month < DATETIME('now', 'start of month'))
).CALCULATE(
    month=sale_month,
    # For each month, create a temporary collection of sales from eligible salespersons.
    eligible_sales_in_month=Sales.WHERE(
        (YEAR(salesperson.hire_date) >= 2022) & (YEAR(salesperson.hire_date) <= 2023)
    ),
    # Calculate PMSPS (Per Month Salesperson Sales count) on the filtered sub-collection.
    PMSPS=COUNT(eligible_sales_in_month),
    # Calculate PMSR (Per Month Sales Revenue) on the filtered sub-collection, defaulting to 0 if no sales.
    PMSR=DEFAULT_TO(SUM(eligible_sales_in_month.sale_price), 0)
).CALCULATE(
    # Select the final columns for the output.
    month,
    PMSPS,
    PMSR
).ORDER_BY(month.ASC())

# Define the date range for the last 6 months, excluding the current month.
start_date = DATETIME('now', 'start of month', '-6 months')
end_date = DATETIME('now', 'start of month')

# First, create a "scaffold" of all months in the last 6 months that have at least one sale.
# This is done by taking all sales, calculating their month, filtering for the date range,
# and then partitioning by month. This approach ensures that months with zero sales
# from the target group but non-zero sales from other groups are included.
sales_with_month = Sales.CALCULATE(
    sale_month=DATETIME(sale_date, 'start of month')
)

recent_months_scaffold = sales_with_month.WHERE(
    (sale_month >= start_date) & (sale_month < end_date)
).PARTITION(
    name="monthly_groups",
    by=(sale_month)
)

# Now, for each month in our scaffold, calculate the required metrics.
# The metrics are calculated by filtering the 'Sales' sub-collection within each partition
# to only include sales from salespersons hired between 2022 and 2023.
sales_metrics = recent_months_scaffold.CALCULATE(
    month=sale_month,
    # PMSPS: Count sales from the target salespersons for the given month.
    PMSPS=COUNT(
        Sales.WHERE(
            (YEAR(salesperson.hire_date) >= 2022) & (YEAR(salesperson.hire_date) <= 2023)
        )
    ),
    # PMSR: Sum the sale_price for the same filtered set of sales.
    # Use DEFAULT_TO to ensure months with no relevant sales show 0.0 instead of NULL.
    PMSR=DEFAULT_TO(
        SUM(
            Sales.WHERE(
                (YEAR(salesperson.hire_date) >= 2022) & (YEAR(salesperson.hire_date) <= 2023)
            ).sale_price
        ),
        0.0
    )
).ORDER_BY(month.ASC())

# The final result is assigned to the variable 'result'.
result = sales_metrics

# We start with the PaymentsReceived collection as it directly gives us access to both the payment_date
# and the related sale_record's sale_date. This also implicitly handles the requirement to
# only consider sales with payments.
payment_days_diff = Dealership.PaymentsReceived.CALCULATE(
    days_difference=DATEDIFF("days", sale_record.sale_date, payment_date)
)

# This provides a single, dealership-wide average payment time.

    avg_days_to_pay=ROUND(AVG(payment_days_diff.days_difference), 2)

# First, for each payment received, calculate the number of days that passed since the sale date.
# We start with the PaymentsReceived collection as it directly gives us access to both the payment_date
# and the related sale_record's sale_date. This also implicitly handles the requirement to
# only consider sales with payments.
payment_days_diff = Dealership.PaymentsReceived.CALCULATE(
    days_difference=DATEDIFF("days", sale_record.sale_date, payment_date)
)

# Then, calculate the average of all these day differences across all payments and round it to 2 decimal places.
# This provides a single, dealership-wide average payment time.
average_payment_time = Dealership.CALCULATE(
    avg_days_to_pay=ROUND(AVG(payment_days_diff.days_difference), 2)
)

# Find cars that went out of inventory and were sold on the same day
cars_sold_same_day = Cars.WHERE(
    HAS(inventory_snapshots.WHERE(is_in_inventory == False)) == 1
).CALCULATE(
    car_make = make,
    car_model = model,
    # Get the date when the car went out of inventory (is_in_inventory = False)
    out_of_inventory_date = inventory_snapshots.WHERE(
        is_in_inventory == False
    ).SINGULAR().snapshot_date,
    # Get the sale information
    sale_price = sale_records.SINGULAR().sale_price,
    sale_date = sale_records.SINGULAR().sale_date
).WHERE(
    # Filter for cars where sale date matches the out of inventory date
    sale_date == out_of_inventory_date
)

# Get the car with the highest sale price
result = cars_sold_same_day.TOP_K(1, by=sale_price.DESC()).CALCULATE(
    make = car_make,
    model = car_model,
    sale_price = sale_price
)

)

# Step 2: Group by year and month to get monthly totals

    name="months",

).CALCULATE(

)

).CALCULATE(

)

# The result is ordered by year and month to present a clear time series.

    payment_year=payment_year,
    payment_month=payment_month,
    total_payments=total_payments,
    mom_change=total_payments - PREV(total_payments, by=(payment_year.ASC(), payment_month.ASC()))
).ORDER_BY(payment_year.ASC(), payment_month.ASC())

# Step 1: Extract year and month from each payment date.
payments_by_month = Dealership.PaymentsReceived.CALCULATE(
    payment_year=YEAR(payment_date),
    payment_month=MONTH(payment_date)
)

# Step 2: Group payments by year and month, and calculate the total payment amount for each group.
# The result is ordered by year and month to prepare for the MoM calculation.
monthly_totals = payments_by_month.PARTITION(
    name="monthly_groups",
    by=(payment_year, payment_month)
).CALCULATE(
    payment_year=payment_year,
    payment_month=payment_month,
    total_payments=SUM(PaymentsReceived.payment_amount)
).ORDER_BY(payment_year.ASC(), payment_month.ASC())

# Step 3: Calculate the Month-over-Month (MoM) change using the PREV window function.
# PREV retrieves the total_payments from the previous month based on the specified order.
result = monthly_totals.CALCULATE(
    payment_year=payment_year,
    payment_month=payment_month,
    total_payments=total_payments,
    mom_change=total_payments - PREV(total_payments, by=(payment_year.ASC(), payment_month.ASC()))
)

[DEBUG] [Q60] Code generated by gemini:
# First, we define the start and end dates for the previous week at the top level.
# The week is considered to start on Monday.
# 'start of week' truncates the current date to the preceding Monday.
# We then subtract 7 days to get the Monday of the previous week,
# and subtract 1 day to get the Sunday of the previous week.
date_boundaries = Dealership.CALCULATE(
    start_of_last_week=DATETIME('now', 'start of week', '-7 days'),
    end_of_last_week=DATETIME('now', 'start of week', '-1 day')
)

# We filter the PaymentsReceived collection to include only payments within the calculated date range.
# Then, we partition the filtered payments by the payment date and payment method to group them.
# Finally, we calculate the sum of payment_amount for each group.
daily_payment_totals = date_boundaries.PaymentsReceived.WHERE(
    (payment_date >= start_of_last_week) & (payment_date <= end_of_last_week)
).PARTITION(
    name="daily_payments_by_method",
    by=(payment_date, payment_method)
).CALCULATE(
    payment_day=payment_date,
    method=payment_method,
    total_amount_received=SUM(PaymentsReceived.payment_amount)
)

# First, we define the start and end dates for the previous week at the top level.
# The week is considered to start on Monday.
# 'start of week' truncates the current date to the preceding Monday.
# We then subtract 7 days to get the Monday of the previous week,
# and subtract 1 day to get the Sunday of the previous week.

    start_of_last_week=DATETIME('now', 'start of week', '-7 days'),
    end_of_last_week=DATETIME('now', 'start of week', '-1 day')
)

# Then, we partition the filtered payments by the payment date and payment method to group them.
# Finally, we calculate the sum of payment_amount for each group.

    (payment_date >= start_of_last_week) & (payment_date <= end_of_last_week)

)

# First, let's get treatments from the last 3 months (excluding current month)
# We'll calculate the month for each treatment and filter accordingly
treatments_with_month = Treatments.CALCULATE(
    treatment_month = JOIN_STRINGS("-", YEAR(start_dt), LPAD(MONTH(start_dt), 2, "0")),
    patient_id = patient_id,
    is_biologic = LOWER(drug.drug_type) == LOWER('biologic')
).WHERE(
    # Filter for last 3 months excluding current month
    (DATEDIFF("months", start_dt, DATETIME('now')) >= 1) & 
    (DATEDIFF("months", start_dt, DATETIME('now')) <= 3)
)

# Now partition by month to count distinct patients
monthly_stats = treatments_with_month.PARTITION(
    name="months", 
    by=treatment_month
).CALCULATE(
    month = treatment_month,
    patient_count = NDISTINCT(Treatments.patient_id),
    biologic_treatment_count = NDISTINCT(Treatments.WHERE(is_biologic == True).patient_id)
)

# Order by month descending to show most recent first
result = monthly_stats.ORDER_BY(month.DESC())

)

    (start_dt >= start_of_3_months_ago) & (start_dt < start_of_current_month)
).CALCULATE(
    treatment_year=YEAR(start_dt),
    treatment_month_num=MONTH(start_dt)
)

# 3. Partition by month and calculate the distinct patient counts, then sort.
monthly_patient_counts = treatments_in_period.PARTITION(
    name="monthly_groups", by=(treatment_year, treatment_month_num)
).CALCULATE(
    month=JOIN_STRINGS("-", treatment_year, treatment_month_num),
    patient_count=NDISTINCT(Treatments.patient_id),
    biologic_treatment_count=NDISTINCT(Treatments.WHERE(LOWER(drug.drug_type) == 'biologic').patient_id)
).ORDER_BY(treatment_year.ASC(), treatment_month_num.ASC())

# First, calculate the date range for the last 12 months excluding current month
# We'll filter treatments that started within this range
treatments_with_month = Treatments.WHERE(
    # Filter for treatments in the last 12 months, excluding current month
    (DATEDIFF("months", start_dt, DATETIME("now")) > 0) & 
    (DATEDIFF("months", start_dt, DATETIME("now")) <= 12)
).CALCULATE(
    # Extract month in yyyy-mm format
    month=JOIN_STRINGS("-", YEAR(start_dt), LPAD(MONTH(start_dt), 2, "0")),
    patient_id=patient_id
)

# Partition by month and calculate PMPD and PMTC
result = treatments_with_month.PARTITION(name="months", by=month).CALCULATE(
    month=month,
    PMPD=NDISTINCT(Treatments.patient_id),  # Distinct patients diagnosed per month
    PMTC=COUNT(Treatments)  # Total treatments per month
).ORDER_BY(month.ASC())

# Define the date boundaries for the last 12 full months, excluding the current month.
date_boundaries = DermTreatment.CALCULATE(
    start_of_current_month=DATETIME('now', 'start of month'),
    start_of_12_months_ago=DATETIME('now', 'start of month', '-12 months')
)

# Filter treatments to the specified period and create a formatted month string for grouping.
treatments_in_period = date_boundaries.Treatments.WHERE(
    (start_dt >= start_of_12_months_ago) & (start_dt < start_of_current_month)
).CALCULATE(
    treatment_month=JOIN_STRINGS("-", YEAR(start_dt), LPAD(MONTH(start_dt), 2, "0"))
)

# Partition by the formatted month and calculate PMPD and PMTC for each month.
monthly_metrics = treatments_in_period.PARTITION(name="monthly_groups", by=treatment_month).CALCULATE(
    month=treatment_month,
    PMPD=NDISTINCT(Treatments.patient_id),
    PMTC=COUNT(Treatments)
).ORDER_BY(treatment_month.ASC())

result = monthly_metrics

# Step 1: For each patient with treatments, find their first treatment year
patients_with_first_year = Patients.WHERE(
    HAS(treatments_received) == 1
).CALCULATE(
    patient_id,
    first_treatment_year=YEAR(MIN(treatments_received.start_dt))
)

# Step 2: Group by year and count new patients
yearly_new_patients = patients_with_first_year.PARTITION(
    name="years", 
    by=first_treatment_year
).CALCULATE(
    year=first_treatment_year,
    num_new_patients=COUNT(Patients)
)

# Step 3: Calculate NPI (increase from previous year)
result = yearly_new_patients.CALCULATE(
    year,
    num_new_patients,
    npi=num_new_patients - PREV(num_new_patients, by=year.ASC(), default=0)
).ORDER_BY(year.ASC())

# Step 1: For each patient with at least one treatment, determine the year of their first treatment.
new_patient_first_treatment_year = DermTreatment.Patients.WHERE(
    HAS(treatments_received) == 1
).CALCULATE(
    first_treatment_year=YEAR(MIN(treatments_received.start_dt))
)

# Step 2: Group patients by their first treatment year and count them to get the number of new patients per year.
new_patients_per_year = new_patient_first_treatment_year.PARTITION(
    name="yearly_cohorts", by=first_treatment_year
).CALCULATE(
    year=first_treatment_year,
    number_of_new_patients=COUNT(Patients)
)

# Step 3: Calculate the year-over-year increase (NPI) and sort the final result by year.
npi_by_year = new_patients_per_year.CALCULATE(
    year=year,
    number_of_new_patients=number_of_new_patients,
    NPI=number_of_new_patients - PREV(number_of_new_patients, by=year.ASC())
).ORDER_BY(year.ASC())

# First, let's get treatments with their start year/month and count matching adverse events
treatments_with_matching_ae = Treatments.CALCULATE(
    drug_id=drug_id,
    start_year=YEAR(start_dt),
    start_month=MONTH(start_dt),
    matching_ae_count=COUNT(adverse_events.WHERE(
        (YEAR(reported_dt) == YEAR(start_dt)) & 
        (MONTH(reported_dt) == MONTH(start_dt))
    ))
)

# Now group by drug and sum up all matching adverse events
drug_ae_counts = treatments_with_matching_ae.PARTITION(
    name="drug_groups", 
    by=drug_id
).CALCULATE(
    drug_id=drug_id,
    total_matching_ae=SUM(treatments_with_matching_ae.matching_ae_count)
)

# Join with drug information and find the top drug
result = drug_ae_counts.CALCULATE(
    drug_id=drug_id,
    drug_name=Drugs.WHERE(drug_id == drug_id).SINGULAR().drug_name,
    num_adverse_events=total_matching_ae
).TOP_K(1, by=num_adverse_events.DESC())

# Filter treatments started in the past 6 months and get specialty info
recent_treatments = Treatments.WHERE(
    DATEDIFF("months", start_dt, DATETIME("now")) <= 6
).CALCULATE(
    doctor_specialty=doctor.speciality,
    drug_amount=tot_drug_amt
)

# Group by specialty and calculate metrics
specialty_stats = recent_treatments.PARTITION(
    name="specialties", 
    by=doctor_specialty
).CALCULATE(
    specialty=doctor_specialty,
    num_treatments=COUNT(Treatments),
    total_drug_amount=SUM(Treatments.tot_drug_amt)
)

# Get top 3 specialties by total drug amount
result = specialty_stats.TOP_K(3, by=total_drug_amount.DESC())

# Define the start date for the last 6 calendar months
six_months_ago = DATETIME('now', '-6 months')

# Filter treatments to the last 6 months and add the doctor's specialty for partitioning
treatments_with_specialty = DermTreatment.Treatments.WHERE(
    start_dt >= six_months_ago
).CALCULATE(
    doc_specialty=doctor.speciality
)

# Partition by specialty, calculate aggregates, and find the top 3
top_3_specialties_by_drug_amount = treatments_with_specialty.PARTITION(
    name="specialty_groups", by=(doc_specialty)
).CALCULATE(
    specialty=doc_specialty,
    number_of_treatments=COUNT(Treatments),
    total_drug_amount=SUM(Treatments.tot_drug_amt)
).TOP_K(3, by=total_drug_amount.DESC())

merchant_cpur = Ewallet.Merchants.CALCULATE(
    merchant_name=name,
    # First, we isolate the successful transactions for each merchant.
    # A transaction is successful if its status is 'success'.
    successful_transactions=transactions_received.WHERE(LOWER(status) == 'success')
).CALCULATE(
    merchant_name=merchant_name,
    # Now, we calculate the CPUR using the successful transactions.
    # We use IFF to handle cases where a merchant has no successful transactions, preventing division by zero.
    CPUR=IFF(
        NDISTINCT(successful_transactions.txid) > 0,
        NDISTINCT(successful_transactions.coupon_id) / NDISTINCT(successful_transactions.txid),
        0.0
    )
)

# Get notifications from US and Canada users for the last 3 weeks excluding current week
us_canada_notifications = Users.WHERE(
    (LOWER(country) == LOWER('US')) | (LOWER(country) == LOWER('Canada'))
).notifications.CALCULATE(
    week_start = DATETIME(created_at, 'start of week'),
    is_weekend = ISIN(DAYNAME(created_at), ('Saturday', 'Sunday'))
).WHERE(
    # Filter for last 3 weeks excluding current week
    (DATEDIFF('weeks', week_start, DATETIME('now', 'start of week')) > 0) &
    (DATEDIFF('weeks', week_start, DATETIME('now', 'start of week')) <= 3)
)

# Partition by week and calculate totals
result = us_canada_notifications.PARTITION(
    name='weekly_groups', 
    by=week_start
).CALCULATE(
    week_start = week_start,
    total_notifications = COUNT(Notifications),
    weekend_notifications = SUM(Notifications.CALCULATE(weekend_count = IFF(is_weekend, 1, 0)).weekend_count)
).ORDER_BY(week_start.DESC())

# Define the time boundaries for the last 3 weeks, excluding the current week.
# This makes the start and end dates available for the subsequent query.
ewallet_context = Ewallet.CALCULATE(
    start_of_current_week=DATETIME('now', 'start of week'),
    start_of_period=DATETIME('now', 'start of week', '-3 weeks')
)

# Filter notifications to include only those sent within the defined time frame
# to users in the US or Canada. Then, for each notification, determine its
# corresponding week and whether it was sent on a weekend.
filtered_notifications = ewallet_context.Notifications.WHERE(
    (created_at >= start_of_period) &
    (created_at < start_of_current_week) &
    ISIN(user.country, ('US', 'Canada'))
).CALCULATE(
    notification_week=DATETIME(created_at, 'start of week'),
    is_weekend=ISIN(DAYNAME(created_at), ('Saturday', 'Sunday'))
)

# Partition the filtered notifications by week and calculate the total and
# weekend notification counts for each week.
weekly_notification_summary = filtered_notifications.PARTITION(
    name='weekly_groups', by=(notification_week)
).CALCULATE(
    week_start_date=notification_week,
    total_notifications=COUNT(Notifications),
    weekend_notifications=SUM(is_weekend)
)

user_avg_balances = recent_balances.PARTITION(

# First, we create a collection of user average balances (AMB) for the specified period.
# We filter the UserBalances to include only records from the last 7 days.
# Then, we partition these records by user_id to group them for each user.
# For each user's group of balances, we calculate their average balance (AMB).
user_ambs = Ewallet.UserBalances.WHERE(
    DATEDIFF("days", updated_at, DATETIME('now')) <= 7
).PARTITION(name="user_groups", by=(user_id)).CALCULATE(
    amb=AVG(UserBalances.balance)
)

# Finally, we calculate the average of all the individual user AMBs calculated in the previous step.
# This gives the overall average AMB for users active in the last week.
average_balance_result = Ewallet.CALCULATE(
    average_balance=AVG(user_ambs.amb)
)

    (DATEDIFF("months", created_at, DATETIME("now")) >= 1) &
    (DATEDIFF("months", created_at, DATETIME("now")) <= 2)
).CALCULATE(
    month=JOIN_STRINGS("-", YEAR(created_at), LPAD(MONTH(created_at), 2, "0")),
    sender_id=sender_id
)

# Partition by month and count distinct senders
result = transaction_info.PARTITION(
    name="monthly_groups", 
    by=month
).CALCULATE(
    month=month,
    pmdau=NDISTINCT(Transactions.sender_id)
).ORDER_BY(month.DESC())

current_month_start = DATETIME('now', 'start of month')

# Filter transactions to the relevant time window and sender type, and pre-calculate the transaction day
transactions_in_window = Ewallet.Transactions.WHERE(
    (sender_type == 0) &
    (created_at >= start_date_limit) &
    (created_at < current_month_start)
).CALCULATE(
    transaction_day=DATETIME(created_at, 'start of day')
)

# Group by day to get the count of Daily Active Users (DAU)
daily_active_users = transactions_in_window.PARTITION(
    name="daily_counts", by=transaction_day
).CALCULATE(
    transaction_day,
    dau=NDISTINCT(Transactions.sender_id)
)

# Pre-calculate the month from the daily data, then group by month to get the average of DAU (PMDAU)
pmdau_by_month = daily_active_users.CALCULATE(
    transaction_month=DATETIME(transaction_day, 'start of month')
).PARTITION(
    name="monthly_avg", by=transaction_month
).CALCULATE(
    month=JOIN_STRINGS('-', YEAR(transaction_month), LPAD(MONTH(transaction_month), 2, '0')),
    pmdau=AVG(daily_counts.dau)
)

# Select the final formatted columns
result = pmdau_by_month.CALCULATE(
    month,
    pmdau
)

[DEBUG] [Q107] Code generated by claude:
# Get transactions from the previous month and calculate STR
result = Ewallet.CALCULATE(
    # Get the start of the previous month
    prev_month_start = DATETIME('now', 'start of month', '-1 month'),
    # Get the start of the current month (end of previous month)
    curr_month_start = DATETIME('now', 'start of month')
).CALCULATE(
    # Filter transactions from the previous month
    prev_month_transactions = Transactions.WHERE(
        (created_at >= prev_month_start) & (created_at < curr_month_start)
    ),
    # Count successful transactions (case insensitive comparison)
    successful_transactions = COUNT(Transactions.WHERE(
        (created_at >= prev_month_start) & 
        (created_at < curr_month_start) & 
        (LOWER(status) == 'success')
    )),
    # Count total transactions
    total_transactions = COUNT(prev_month_transactions)
).CALCULATE(
    # Calculate STR as a percentage
    str_percentage = IFF(
        total_transactions > 0,
        100.0 * successful_transactions / total_transactions,
        0.0
    )
)

# Define the start of the current month and the start of the previous month
start_of_current_month = DATETIME('now', 'start of month')
start_of_previous_month = DATETIME(start_of_current_month, '-1 month')

# Filter transactions to include only those from the previous month
transactions_in_last_month = Ewallet.Transactions.WHERE(
    (created_at >= start_of_previous_month) & (created_at < start_of_current_month)
)

# Calculate the number of successful and total transactions
transaction_counts = Ewallet.CALCULATE(
    successful_transactions=COUNT(transactions_in_last_month.WHERE(LOWER(status) == 'success')),
    total_transactions=COUNT(transactions_in_last_month)
)

# Calculate the Success Transaction Rate (STR) and select only that field
wallet_str_previous_month = transaction_counts.CALCULATE(
    str=IFF(total_transactions > 0, successful_transactions / total_transactions, 0.0)

    curr_month_start = DATETIME('now', 'start of month')
).CALCULATE(
    # Filter transactions from the previous month
    prev_month_transactions = Transactions.WHERE(
        (created_at >= prev_month_start) & (created_at < curr_month_start)
    ),
    # Count successful transactions (case insensitive comparison)
    successful_transactions = COUNT(Transactions.WHERE(
        (created_at >= prev_month_start) & 
        (created_at < curr_month_start) & 
        (LOWER(status) == 'success')
    )),
    # Count total transactions
    total_transactions = COUNT(prev_month_transactions)
).CALCULATE(
    # Calculate STR as a percentage
    str_percentage = IFF(
        total_transactions > 0,
        100.0 * successful_transactions / total_transactions,
        0.0
    )
)

# First, filter transactions to include only those made by active users in 2023 that were successful.
# A 'transaction_month' field is created by truncating the creation date to the start of the month.
transactions_in_2023 = Ewallet.Transactions.WHERE(
    (YEAR(created_at) == 2023) &
    (LOWER(status) == 'completed') &
    (HAS(sending_user) == 1) &
    (LOWER(sending_user.status) == 'active')
).CALCULATE(
    transaction_month=DATETIME(created_at, 'start of month')
)

# Partition the filtered transactions by month.
# For each month, count the number of distinct users who sent money.
monthly_active_senders = transactions_in_2023.PARTITION(
    name="monthly_transactions",
    by=(transaction_month)
).CALCULATE(
    month=transaction_month,
    active_users_count=NDISTINCT(Transactions.sending_user.uid)
).ORDER_BY(month.ASC())

).transactions_sent.WHERE(

).CALCULATE(
    user_id=sender_id,
    month_date=DATETIME(created_at, 'start of month')
)

# Partition by month and count distinct users

    name="months", 
    by=month_date
).CALCULATE(

    active_users=NDISTINCT(active_users_transactions_2023.user_id)
).ORDER_BY(month.ASC())

# First, let's get users with their country and filter for those who sent transactions with sender_type = 0
users_with_transactions = Users.WHERE(
    HAS(transactions_sent.WHERE(sender_type == 0)) == 1
).CALCULATE(
    user_country = country,
    user_id = uid,
    total_sent = SUM(transactions_sent.WHERE(sender_type == 0).amount)
)

# Now partition by country to aggregate the data
country_stats = users_with_transactions.PARTITION(
    name="countries", 
    by=user_country
).CALCULATE(
    country = user_country,
    num_distinct_users = COUNT(Users),
    total_transaction_amount = SUM(Users.total_sent)
)

# Get the top 5 countries by total transaction amount
result = country_stats.TOP_K(5, by=total_transaction_amount.DESC())

).CALCULATE(

    total_sent = SUM(transactions_sent.WHERE(sender_type == 0).amount)
)

)

# First, identify all snapshots on the earliest date in 2023.
# This is done by filtering for the year 2023, then ranking the snapshots by date in ascending order.
# Using RANKING with allow_ties=True ensures that all snapshots from the same earliest date are selected.
# We then filter for rank 1 to get only the earliest snapshots.
earliest_snapshots_in_2023 = Ewallet.UserSettingSnapshots.WHERE(
    YEAR(snapshot_date) == 2023
).CALCULATE(
    rank_by_date=RANKING(by=snapshot_date.ASC(), allow_ties=True)
).WHERE(rank_by_date == 1)

# Next, calculate the average daily and monthly transaction limits from this filtered set of snapshots.
# The final result will contain the two requested average values.
result = Ewallet.CALCULATE(
    avg_tx_limit_daily=AVG(earliest_snapshots_in_2023.tx_limit_daily),
    avg_tx_limit_monthly=AVG(earliest_snapshots_in_2023.tx_limit_monthly)
)
